Independent review of run r-20261009T120429823041-alternate-chains-jt60sa at head 96d50e7ce86ede2ccf70891fc8e4d5d84cf20c37 against base 51dc23fbc8d4f85e782ad6a094b3d9d50fba65be, the second of the plan section-20 nodes. The node declares, on each JT-60SA pf_active coil-current rule whose evidence names it, the counterpart acquisition chain as an alternate_source, so a draft bound to the LKAT chain where the hand-built map serves the HiTe chain (EF1-EF5), or the HiTe chain where it serves the LKAT chain (EF6), scores as a chain choice under chain_differs rather than as a mapping error under conflicting.

Goal fidelity. Read plan section 20 and its two-node ordering comment, the prior node's merged mechanism (SignalRule.alternate_sources and handoff_score._measure's chain_differs branch), the reviewed dispatch and manifest, base 51dc23fb and head 96d50e7c, the single commit with its complete diff, the reviewed node's gate and negative-control logs, the fragment, and the development map /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/imas-ambix/maps/jt-60sa/maps/pf_active.json. All ten pf_active coil-current rules carry one alternate each (CS1-CS4, EF1-EF5 LKAT serving HiTe; EF6 HiTe serving LKAT), and the rescore the fragment quotes moves pf_active/coil from conflicting 6 to conflicting 0 / chain_differs 6, which the head-arm test asserts.

Independent verification. The reviewed node's declared gate tests/test_maps_cli.py was re-run by this review at the reviewed head over a scratch extraction of 96d50e7c with the machine maps linked: 40 passed, EXIT=0, module imas_ambix.maps_cli resolving to that extraction. A base arm over a scratch extraction of 51dc23fb with the reviewed node's test file at head kept drives the two new column tests red -- test_score_handoff_prints_a_conflicting_column and test_score_handoff_prints_a_chain_differs_column, 2 failed and 38 passed, EXIT=1 -- so the maps_cli.py change is guarded and not restated; the real-map rescore test passes at base too, because the chain_differs mechanism landed with the prior node.

Reachability. The map declaration is read through handoff_score._measure's alternate_targets lookup (the imported rule's (source_group, source_array) against prior.alternate_keys on the same target), so runtime code reaches it through the score rather than through a test alone; the printed columns read the row's own chain_differs and cross_structure lists.

Record. No blocking defect. Three follow-ons and a cosmetic: the reviewed run is unarmed, so this review supplies the two-arm delta (empty); the map deliverable is untracked and needs a maps release, and its guard skips when the bundle is absent; the maps_cli.py column change is section-10/19 surface granted by the dispatch; and the fragment has no trailing newline.
